name: Robinhood
summary: Candidates report a recruiter call, a technical screen (often run through Karat, sometimes CodeSignal), then an onsite of coding, system design, a past project review and a hiring manager round. Coding reports mix medium LeetCode-style problems with practical ones such as dependency graphs and share trading.

rounds.name: Recruiter call
rounds.what: Work history, interest in Robinhood and role fit.

rounds.name: Technical phone screen
rounds.what: About 30 minutes of coding, usually one or two medium problems, plus short system design questions; often run by Karat.

rounds.name: Onsite coding
rounds.what: Data structures and algorithms in CoderPad, with correctness weighted over scalability.

rounds.name: System design
rounds.what: Usually two design rounds, one broad and one focused, often tied to trading or fintech products.

rounds.name: Past project review
rounds.what: Walk through a prepared diagram of a past project and go deep on decisions.

rounds.name: Hiring manager
rounds.what: Behavioural and culture fit through role-related scenarios.

tips: Aim for correct, bug-free code first; reports say correctness matters more than scale in coding rounds.
Prepare your past project diagram early and be ready to defend each decision.
Practise graph problems such as dependency counting and topological sort.
Know Robinhood's products and core values, and why you want to work in fintech.
Karat interviewers are contractors, so save team questions for later rounds.
